title: Dumping Ground "utils" / "common" Module
pattern: A central module named `utils`, `common`, or `helpers` contains a variety of static functions that operate on completely different domains and levels of abstraction.
why_bad: It lacks any functional cohesion. It serves as a shortcut that prevents developers from carefully deciding where a behavior truly belongs, leading to circular imports and an unmaintainable codebase.
detection: A file or module contains multiple public functions that do not share any common data parameters or represent a unified domain concept.
counterexample: Highly specialized mathematical or algorithm utility modules that operate within a single mathematical domain (e.g., `matrix_utils`).
source: *John Ousterhout - A Philosophy of Software Design, Chapter 4 / Steve McConnell - Code Complete, Chapter 6, Section "Logical Cohesion"*
